what: ARMS-r3 section 8 (P5) KP add-on decision: ARMS.md step 6 applied to the counted ABAB Kp-1 (K#3), KP-1 (KP#1), Kp-2 (K#4), KP-2 (KP#2) in results/2026-09-26-serve-r3/. KPsafe-1 (the uncounted s8 safety boot) and the earlier boots of the same K config (K-1, K-2, CUR-1, CUR-2) appear only as labelled context. Computed by decision-addons-compute.py.txt from the raw per-boot files through the per-boot readers of decision-bundle-compute.py.txt; stdlib only.

sources: ARMS-r3 section 8 (P5): 'K#3, KP#1, K#4, KP#2 (K = the promoted bundle), same gates as P2. Quality quick on both KP boots.' 'If KP fails the gate, split it: K+{PM_QOS, WKV_TP} against K first ..., then the rest one at a time.'
ARMS-r3 section 5 (the P2 gates) and section 10 (quality)
rule.primary_metric: prose_median_ms_per_step (four_numbers prose cell, 9 runs) and prose_long c=1 median_ms_per_step (5 runs), per boot; arm value = median of its 2 boots. Both cells are bench_decode.py at temperature 0.
rule.matched_acceptance: ARMS.md: 'the A and B per-boot median_run_acceptance_len must overlap. If they do not, the arm changed drafting; gate on prose_long c=1 tok/s instead with the same noise rule.' ARMS-r3 s5 adds L.A.I.L tok/s to that fallback.
rule.noise: the larger boot-to-boot spread (max-min of the per-boot values) of the two arms; pass = median improvement > noise AND every KP boot beats the K median
also_required: non-inferiority: pp_warm/pp_novel 8k/32k, prose_long c=2 aggregate, warm-prefix not worse than K by more than the larger spread (the P2 decision's reading; the K-spread-only reading is also recorded)
honest cells, disarm_scan and gpu_guard clean, e2e rc 0, boot floors, on every counted boot
quality quick passes on both KP boots

notes: No boot is VOID: gpu_guard --check rc 0 (0 FOREIGN) and no CONTAMINATED marker on all five P5 boots.
The spark2 GPU lock holder was refused by the permission layer on Kp-1 and KP-1 (the lock was free at precheck and after stop, and the spark2 guard was clean). It was held on KPsafe-1, Kp-2 and KP-2.

Slow L.A.I.L runs inside clean boots were kept as measured: Kp-1 run 5 (53.73 ms/step), KP-1 run 10 (50.99), Kp-2 runs 2/3/5 (55.52/52.88/53.26), KP-2 run 5 (58.77). The per-boot medians are the gate values.

Greedy smokes (smoke_chat '323', smoke_vision 'Red') are byte-identical on all five boots. The only correctness output that differs from Kp-1 is prose_sanity, which is sampled and also differs between Kp-1 and Kp-2.

Model loading per rank [head, worker], quoted from the gitignored .run-state audit logs. Kp-1 (K): 75.58/75.58 GiB, 429.76/268.55 s; KP-1 (KP): 75.43/75.43 GiB, 373.21/373.39 s; Kp-2 (K): 75.58/75.58 GiB, 433.74/262.61 s; KP-2 (KP): 75.43/75.43 GiB, 369.76/368.13 s; KPsafe-1 (KP): 75.43/75.43 GiB, 371.32/371.66 s. KP loads the same time on both ranks. That is consistent with WKV_TP's post-load collective self-check making the ranks wait for each other, which is not verified. Why the head loads ~60 s faster under KP is not established. run.sh start to vLLM start, from the notes.txt of each boot: KPsafe-1 526 s, KP-1 539 s, KP-2 547 s; Kp-1 584 s, Kp-2 590 s. Not a gate metric.

projection_vs_measured.source: ARMS-r3 s11: KP add-ons -2.4..-7.1 ms/step at c=1 (MHC_OVERLAP -0.6..-0.75, WKV_TP -0.55..-0.59 with DENSE_GEMV on, PM_QOS -0.7..-2.0, EAGER_TWIN -0.5..-3.1, L2_PREFETCH -0.07..-0.63); microbench, first order, serve-untested
projection_vs_measured.reading: Every c=1 cell sits above the projected range (a smaller saving than the low end, -2.4). The c=2 cells range from a saving (prose_long c=2) to no change (bench prose / structured c=2, inside their noise).

greedy_cross_arm_divergence.note: quality_quick selfcons: 12 greedy prompts x 128 tokens, 2 runs per boot. Hazard = divergences per token at risk (first-divergence events / tokens up to and including the first divergence), pooled over every run pair of the named boots. If the add-ons changed greedy numerics, KP-vs-K would diverge more than K-vs-K across boots.

reading: Quality quick passes on every component on both KP boots (and on KPsafe-1 and both K boots).

tools.exact_args reads 20/22 on KP-1, Kp-1 and Kp-2 (t01 and t09 called with {}) and 21/22 on KP-2 and KPsafe-1 (t09). The 20/22 readings pass the 0.9545 limit only by the gate's one-item Wilson slack. The same pattern shows on both arms, so it is not an add-on effect.

Greedy numerics: the KP-vs-K cross-arm divergence hazard equals the K-vs-K cross-boot hazard (the serve is not deterministic at temperature 0 from boot to boot or run to run; every boot's own A/A hazard is non-zero). This is consistent with the add-ons being bit-exact in the serve, at the resolution the serve's own nondeterminism allows.

decision.verdict: NOT PROMOTED: none of the five add-ons joins the defaults. The promoted config stays the 10 K envs. ms/step: KP is lower than K beyond the noise on every c=1 cell and on prose_long c=2, and every KP boot beats the K median. Four prose c=1 -1.325 (noise 0.561), prose_long c=1 -1.81 (noise 0.333). ARMS.md step 6 uses that ms/step as primary only at matched acceptance, and the per-boot median_run_acceptance_len intervals do not overlap on either primary cell. Four prose: K [2.5897, 2.5844], KP [2.525, 2.5769]. Prose_long c=1: K [2.1505, 2.117], KP [2.0729, 2.0938]. So the rule gates on tok/s. prose_long c=1 tok/s improves 0.198 against noise 0.718, and KP-2 (43.816) is below the K median (43.977). L.A.I.L tok/s improves 1.459 against noise 1.594. Both fallback gates fail. Non-inferiority, honest cells, guards and quality quick all pass. The speed gate is the only check that fails.
why_the_rule_is_applied_as_written: The fallback exists for arms that trade acceptance for step time, where lower ms/step does not mean faster output. On the two primary cells that is the pattern measured here. prose_long c=1: ms/step -1.81 (-3.71%), per-boot acceptance -0.0504 (-2.36%; K median 2.1338, KP median 2.0834), tok/s +0.198 (+0.45%). Four prose c=1: ms/step -1.325 (-2.77%), tok/s +0.075 (+0.14%).

The evidence on whether the acceptance gap is noise or a drafting change is mixed, and it is not the rule's test. (1) Per run, the gap is not significant. Mann-Whitney on the counted boots: four prose p 0.21671, prose_long c=1 p 0.79111. All three KP boots against all six boots of the K config on this pack: p 0.16047 and 0.35963. (2) Per boot, against those six K-config boots, prose_long c=1 KP-1 and KP-2 are the two lowest of 8 (exact one-sided rank-sum p 0.0357; with KPsafe-1, 3 of 9, p 0.0833). Four prose gives p 0.2143. No correction for testing three cells is applied. (3) Greedy KP-vs-K divergence hazard is 0.0183, against K-vs-K 0.01832 and KP-vs-KP 0.01844 across boots. (4) structured c=1 is at exactly matched acceptance ([3.961] on every run of every boot). There ms/step moves -1.563 (noise 0.268; 18/18 KP runs below every K-config run) and tok/s moves +2.893 (noise 0.512), both beyond the noise. (1), (3) and (4) point to noise, and (2) is borderline on prose_long. None of them is the step-6 test. Choosing a different test after seeing the result is what the fixed rule is there to prevent. Changing the rule is for the protocol owner, not for this decision.

Correction to the KP-2 stage note: the four prose and prose_long cells are not sampled. bench_decode.py sends temperature 0; only L.A.I.L runs at t=0.2. Their run-to-run acceptance spread comes from the serve's own nondeterminism at temperature 0: the within-boot greedy A/A hazard is non-zero on every boot of both arms.
context_observations: pp_warm_8k passes non-inferiority against the larger spread (delta -22.65, noise 34.8). It fails the reading against K's own spread (22.5) by 0.15. KP's spread comes from KP-1's low median. Per run, 3/9 KP-arm runs (KP-1, KP-2, KPsafe-1) fall below the lowest of the 18 K-config runs (734.2): KP-1 [680.3, 754.5, 723.2], KPsafe-1 [739.4, 688.8, 781.9]. KP-2 [776.2, 758.0, 746.9] has none. Mann-Whitney p 0.14268. Recorded, not a gate failure; a KP_p boot or the s8 split would show whether an add-on touches warm-prefix prefill.

bench prose c=2 aggregate tok/s: K [85.558, 85.357], KP [84.596, 82.762], delta -1.779 against noise 1.834, so inside the noise. Both KP boots are below the K median. bench prose c=2 ms/step is -0.146 (noise 1.4) and structured c=2 ms/step is 0.117 (noise 1.239). Only prose_long c=2 ms/step (-1.843, noise 0.492) shows the c=1 pattern at c=2. structured c=2 aggregate tok/s +3.214 (noise 0.319) and prose_long c=2 aggregate +1.307 (noise 0.206) pass the noise rule.

L.A.I.L runs at t=0.2 and its per-boot acceptance overlaps (K [2.1269, 2.0727], KP [2.1136, 2.1179]). Its ms/step moves -1.732 against noise 0.082, but L.A.I.L is not a step-6 primary cell. Its tok/s gate misses: +1.459 against noise 1.594, a noise set by Kp-2's three slow runs (per-boot [43.493, 41.899]).

The s8 mechanism check was not run: 86 mhc_det_gemm_t8 + 86 mhc_det_norm_coef on a second stream inside each AllReduce, with the ncclDevKernel_AllReduce median not rising by more than ~7 us. It needs a KP_p profile boot.
DSV41_MHC_DET_OVERLAP=1.verdict: NOT PROMOTED. KP did not pass the P5 gate as a set (step 6 as written, see decision), and no evidence isolates this add-on, so it cannot be promoted alone. next_steps_per_s8: s8 says that if KP fails the gate, it is split: an ABAB of K+{PM_QOS, WKV_TP} against K first (the two highest-confidence add-ons), then the other three one at a time, as in comm/serve_arm_plan.txt and mhc-det/serve_validation_plan.txt.

The s8 KP_p profile boot against K_p is still owed. It gives the per-add-on attribution that no counted boot provides. It also settles the EAGER_TWIN graphUsageMode question and whether L2_PREFETCH or MHC_OVERLAP slows the all-reduce (s12). If it does, s8 says to retry with DSV41_AR_L2_PREFETCH_MIB=5.5.

For the protocol owner: for levers that are bit-exact by construction, should matched acceptance be judged on the pooled per-run distribution, or on a cell whose acceptance is fixed (structured c=1), instead of on 2 per-boot medians? Measured here: KP is -1.3..-1.9 ms/step at c=1, beyond the noise. Under the current rule it does not promote. That rule change does not happen in this decision.
